sections.text: Transmission Lines

Technical 
 Procedure

Equipment:Dead Ends 
 for Monometallic Conductors
Introduction

This document outlines the equipment inspection I1, 
which must be performed on an annually bases as indicated by Y1 in the title 
block.

The first draft initiated by eng. Abd El-Satar, 
EEHC technical inspection & quality control head sector, and from TL 
instructions document, 
this document certified by by eng. MPIS 
zone coordinators

Safety 
Precautions

items:
A work permit must be issued and the maintenance staff 
 should carry the suitable safety category.

Maintenance staff should be well trained, qualified or 
 directly supervised by some one who is.

Safety fence with caution marks surrounding the work area 
 is required.

Wear the personal protective equipment must used as safety 
 shoes, safety helmet, earplug, and gloves pairs...etc

sections.text:
Tools and 
Equipment

Safety and healthy equipment as 
 safety harnesses, cotton suit,... etc
Work to be Carried out
Be sure that the die corresponds to the right size
Make certain that the end body and jumper terminal bores are thoroughly clean

Be sure that the conductor end is not damaged if it is cut off the damaged 
portion

Clean thoroughly all strands of conductor portion having to be compressed. This is particularly important and 
is to be made by unwinding the 
various wire layers, especially in case of greassed or old and in the 
first case a suitable solvent may be used in the latter case use emery cloth 
or metallic brush having steel wires 2 to 3/10 of mm long

Put a reference mark on the conductor at a distance 
equal to the length of dead end body bore, then insert the conductor into the 
dead end and slip it in thoroughly (fig. 17-a) making sure that above mark is 
reached

Compress the dead end starting from the reference close to the lug (fig. 17-b) 
and continue compressions toward the conductor overlapping one half of each compression 
being sure every time that the two half dies barrel together

Clean accurately as mentioned at point 4 all wires of the end of conductor 
having to be put into the jumper terminal

Insert the conductor thoroughly into the jumper terminal then start compressing 
from lug side (fig. 17-c) going on according to previous instructions

Clean perfectly the contact surfaces of dead end lug and of jumper terminal 
abrade them with emery - cloth or metallic brush then bolt the two parts with 
each other

sections.text: Midspan Joints for Monometallic Conductors
Be sure that the die corresponds to the right size
Make certain that the joint bore is perfectly clean

Be sure that the conductor ends to joint are not damaged if they are cut off the 
damaged portion

Clean thoroughly all strands of conductor parts having to be compressed. This is 
particularly important and is to be made by unwinding the various strand layers 
especially in case of a greassed or old and blackened conductor. In the first 
case, a suitable solvent may be used in the latter case use emery - cloth or a 
metallic brush having steel wires 2 to 3/10 of mm. long

Put a reference mark on each conductor at a distance equal to half the length of 
the joint then put the conductors into the joint making them slip up to the 
marks made before (fig. 18-a)

Compress the joint starting from the centre (fig. 18-b) and continue compressing 
alternately toward one end and toward the other overlapping one half of each 
compression making every time sure that the two half dies barrel together

case, a suitable solvent may be used in the latter case use emery - cloth or a 
metallic brush having steel wires 2 to 3/10 of mm. long

Put a reference mark on each conductor at a distance equal to half the length of

marks made before (fig. 18-a)

alternately toward one end and toward the other overlapping one half of each 
compression making every time sure that the two half dies barrel together
